name: The call stack
summary: Each function call pushes a frame holding its arguments, locals, and return address, and the frame pops when the call returns.

name: Recursion
summary: A recursive function solves a problem by calling itself on smaller instances of the same problem and combining the results.

name: Base cases
summary: A base case answers the smallest inputs directly so every chain of recursive calls is guaranteed to stop.

name: Tracing recursion
summary: Tracing follows each recursive call and return by hand, often as a call tree, to predict what a recursive function outputs.

name: Complexity of recursive functions
summary: The time and space cost of a recursive function comes from counting the calls in its call tree, the work per call, and the maximum stack depth.

name: Memoization
summary: Memoization caches the result of each call by its arguments so repeated subproblems are computed only once.

name: Top-down dynamic programming
summary: Top-down DP writes the natural recursive solution and adds memoization so overlapping subproblems collapse into polynomial work.

name: DP states and transitions
summary: A DP solution defines a state that captures each subproblem and a transition that computes a state's answer from smaller states.

name: Bottom-up dynamic programming
summary: Bottom-up DP fills a table of states in an order where every dependency is already computed, replacing recursion with iteration.
